clients.name: Lumen Analytics
clients.stack: Next.js 14, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, ECharts via echarts-for-react (every dashboard is canvas charts), Postgres
constraints: Charts are the product: any chart regression is a P1 incident
Customers export charts to PNG for board decks, and exports must stay print-friendly on a light background
Every UI change ships behind a feature flag with a staged rollout

memories.request: Let customers export any dashboard chart as a PNG for board decks
memories.solution: Used the chart library's built-in image export at 2x pixel ratio instead of screenshotting the page
memories.what_broke: Exports had transparent backgrounds that turned black when pasted into some slide tools
memories.fix: Set an explicit white background on the export only, leaving the on-screen chart unchanged
memories.outcome: Shipped in a week; export is now the second most-used feature

memories.request: Speed up dashboards that render 40+ charts
memories.solution: Mounted charts lazily as they scroll into view and sampled very large series before drawing
memories.what_broke: Charts that mounted inside hidden tabs rendered at zero width
memories.fix: Resized each chart when its tab becomes visible
memories.outcome: Dashboard load time dropped from 9s to 2.5s

memories.request: Add SAML single sign-on for enterprise customers
memories.solution: Integrated SAML through our auth provider and mapped identity-provider groups to workspace roles
memories.what_broke: Users whose emails differed only by letter case got duplicate accounts
memories.fix: Normalized emails to lowercase before every account lookup

clients.name: Pinecrest Pay
clients.stack: Nuxt 3 (Vue), SCSS with design tokens, Node.js API, payment processor's hosted card-entry iframe
constraints: PCI scope: no new third-party scripts on payment pages
Every partner credit union has its own brand theme
Releases go through a two-week compliance review

memories.request: Per-partner color themes so each credit union sees its own brand
memories.solution: Generated one set of CSS variables per partner from our design tokens and swapped the set at login
memories.what_broke: The payment processor's hosted card-entry iframe ignored our CSS variables and stayed default blue
memories.fix: Passed the partner's colors through the processor's iframe styling options when the iframe mounts
memories.outcome: 14 partners branded with zero custom code per partner. Lesson: CSS variables stop at iframe and third-party boundaries

memories.request: Speed up monthly statement PDF generation
memories.solution: Moved PDF rendering to a background queue and cached each partner's statement template
memories.what_broke: Brand fonts were missing in the containerized renderer, so statements fell back to a default serif font
memories.fix: Bundled the brand fonts into the renderer image
memories.outcome: Statement generation went from 6 hours to 40 minutes

memories.request: Add two-factor authentication to member logins
memories.solution: Authenticator-app codes with recovery codes, SMS only as a fallback
memories.what_broke: Members who changed phones got locked out and flooded support
memories.fix: Added self-serve recovery through a verified email with a 24-hour cooldown
memories.outcome: Account takeover reports dropped to zero; support volume was back to normal within two weeks

clients.name: Harbor Health
clients.stack: Next.js, Tailwind CSS, Radix UI primitives; no charting library (results are shown as accessible tables)
constraints: WCAG 2.1 AA is a legal requirement: 4.5:1 contrast for text, 3:1 for UI components
Every UI change gets a screen-reader pass (NVDA and VoiceOver) before release
Respect OS settings: prefers-color-scheme and prefers-reduced-motion
No patient data in client-side logs or analytics

memories.request: Add dark mode to the patient portal
memories.solution: Moved every color into CSS variables at the root, swapped them with a theme attribute, defaulted to the OS preference and remembered the user's choice
memories.what_broke: Nothing. It shipped in about 2 hours
memories.fix: None needed; we re-ran the contrast checker on both themes before release
memories.outcome: Shipped the same day, passed the WCAG AA audit in both themes, zero bug reports

memories.request: Make appointment booking usable with a screen reader
memories.solution: Rebuilt the date picker on accessible primitives with proper roles and live announcements
memories.what_broke: Focus jumped back to the top of the page after every step
memories.fix: Moved focus to each step's heading when the step changes
memories.outcome: Passed the external accessibility audit; booking completion rose 18% among screen-reader users

memories.request: Show lab result trends to patients
memories.solution: Showed trends as accessible tables with plain-language summaries instead of adding a chart library
memories.what_broke: An early canvas chart prototype was invisible to screen readers
memories.fix: Dropped the canvas chart for a semantic table plus a small trend image with alt text
memories.outcome: Audit passed; patients preferred the plain-language summaries

memories.request: Add an inactivity timeout for shared hospital kiosks
memories.solution: Warned two minutes before logout with an accessible dialog and an extend button
memories.what_broke: Screen-reader users could not reach the extend button before the session ended
memories.fix: The warning dialog now takes focus, and the warning window grew to five minutes
memories.outcome: Met the hospital security policy with no accessibility complaints

clients.name: Atlas Freight
clients.stack: Go microservices, gRPC, Postgres, Kafka; public REST API and webhooks only, no customer-facing web UI
constraints: Public API changes must be backwards compatible and versioned
SOC 2: every change needs a reviewed pull request and an audit trail

memories.request: Add rate limiting to the public API
memories.solution: Token bucket per API key at the gateway, with the remaining quota returned in response headers
memories.what_broke: One customer's retry storm hit the limit, and their retries multiplied the load
memories.fix: Returned Retry-After headers and documented exponential backoff in the API guide
memories.outcome: No more API brownouts during peak shipping season

memories.request: Deliver shipment status updates through webhooks
memories.solution: Outbox table plus a delivery worker with signed payloads and retries
memories.what_broke: Out-of-order deliveries made customers display stale statuses
memories.fix: Added sequence numbers and told customers to ignore older events
memories.outcome: Webhooks now carry 80% of status traffic and polling dropped sharply

memories.request: Upgrade the rates database to a new Postgres version without downtime
memories.solution: Logical replication to the new cluster, then a 30-second read-only cutover
memories.what_broke: Sequences were not replicated, so the first inserts after cutover collided
memories.fix: Bumped every sequence past its current maximum id before the cutover
memories.outcome: Cutover finished in 30 seconds during business hours

clients.name: Ridgeline Logistics
clients.stack: React 18, Vite, TypeScript, ECharts via echarts-for-react, Mapbox GL
constraints: Dispatchers work night shifts on wall-mounted screens, so glare matters
The dashboard must stay live during a shift: no full page reloads
Ops leadership signs off on any visual change to the live map

memories.request: Add dark mode to the fleet dashboard for night-shift dispatchers
memories.solution: Moved our colors into CSS variables and flipped them with a theme toggle, the usual pattern
memories.what_broke: The chart library ignored the CSS variables. ECharts paints on canvas from JavaScript options, so axis labels, legends and gridlines stayed dark-on-dark and unreadable, and tooltips stayed bright white. Dispatchers reported broken charts on the first night shift
memories.fix: Registered light and dark chart themes built from the same design tokens and passed the active one through the chart component's theme prop, re-rendering charts when the theme toggles
memories.outcome: Rolled back for two days, then reshipped with the theme prop; no chart issues since. Lesson: CSS variables reach DOM and SVG, not canvas charts

memories.request: Show 2,000 live trucks on the map without freezing
memories.solution: Replaced per-truck DOM markers with a clustered GPU layer and throttled position updates to once per second
memories.what_broke: Clicking a cluster near the screen edge zoomed to the wrong place
memories.fix: Used the map library's cluster expansion zoom instead of a fixed zoom step
memories.outcome: The map holds 60fps with more than 2,000 vehicles

memories.request: Export a shift report as CSV
memories.solution: Streamed the CSV from the API instead of building it in the browser
memories.what_broke: Spreadsheet apps mangled timestamps and dropped leading zeros from truck IDs
memories.fix: Wrote ISO timestamps and quoted the ID columns
memories.outcome: Dispatch leads use it every morning
